result.markdown:
Yes. For a **slip-and-fall in a Hobart shopping centre**, you’re generally looking for a lawyer experienced in **Tasmanian public liability/personal injury**, rather than a general commercial lawyer.

I wouldn’t call anyone objectively “the best” without knowing the circumstances, but based on the firms I found, these are the ones I’d shortlist:

| Firm | Why I’d consider them | Local signal |
|---|---|---|
| **LHD Lawyers Hobart** | Specifically handles Hobart public-liability/slip-and-fall claims. Their Hobart team includes Tanya To, an accredited personal-injury specialist, and they advertise no-win-no-fee arrangements. [www.lhd.com.au](https://www.lhd.com.au/office-location/tas/hobart/public-liability-claims/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) | 4.8/5 from 127 reviews |
| **Slater and Gordon Lawyers Hobart** | Has a dedicated Hobart public-liability practice and explicitly lists **slipping/falling at shopping centres or supermarkets** as the type of claim they handle. They offer an obligation-free initial appointment and no-win-no-fee arrangements. [www.slatergordon.com.au](https://www.slatergordon.com.au/personal-injury/public-liability/public-liability-lawyers-in-hobart?utm_source=chatgpt.com) | Established national personal-injury practice |
| **Blumers Personal Injury Lawyers** | A Hobart personal-injury specialist with a strong local review profile. | 4.9/5 from 34 reviews |
| **Firths The Compensation Lawyers** | Specifically handles public-place/slip-and-fall claims and advertises a no-win-no-fee guarantee, with a Hobart office. [www.firths.com.au](https://www.firths.com.au/offices/41/hobart?utm_source=chatgpt.com) | Dedicated compensation practice |


### My practical shortlist

I'd get **two or three initial assessments**, rather than immediately signing with the first firm. In particular, I'd speak to **LHD and Slater & Gordon**, then compare their answers on:

1. **Whether they think the shopping centre/occupier was actually negligent** — merely falling isn't automatically enough; you generally need to establish breach of duty and causation.
2. **Who is potentially liable** — shopping-centre owner, centre manager, individual retailer, cleaning contractor, etc.
3. **Whether CCTV and incident reports have been preserved.**
4. **Exactly what “no win, no fee” means**, including counsel's fees, medical/expert costs and any uplift or other deductions.
5. **What they think the claim could realistically be worth**, once your injuries and prognosis are known.

### Do this now if the fall was recent

This is particularly important with a shopping-centre accident: **ask the centre in writing to preserve all CCTV footage covering the accident, surrounding area and relevant entrances/exits**, and keep your own photographs of the location/hazard if possible.

Also keep:
- the incident report/reference number;
- names and contact details of witnesses;
- photographs of the hazard and your injuries;
- medical records and receipts;
- evidence of lost wages;
- emails/messages you've exchanged with the centre.

Tasmania's limitation legislation generally provides a **3-year period for personal-injury negligence actions, running from discoverability**, although there are exceptions and extensions. Don't rely on that period as a reason to wait—evidence such as CCTV can disappear much sooner.
